_sources.role: sessional hymns, canon troparia (1st canon), ikos, Ode 9 megalynaria refrains
_sources.label: St-Sergius Pentecostarion (yy register)

_meta._note: Single-canon structure per OCA practice (1st Canon Tone 5 by John the Monk); Tone 4 katavasiae borrowed from the 2nd Canon of Pentecost. OCA publishes only irmoi for the canon; troparia + sessional hymns + ikos sourced from St-Sergius Pentecostarion. Magnificat NOT sung; before Ode 9 irmos+troparia the megalynarion 'Magnify, O my soul, Christ the Giver of Life…' is sung as a leading refrain. "Having beheld the Resurrection" IS sung at Ascension Matins per OCA rubric (includeHavingBeheld: true), unlike Pentecost. Mixed registers — irmoi/lauds OCA tt, troparia/sessional hymns St-Sergius yy/archaic.

troparion.text:
Thou didst ascend in glory, O Christ our God,
granting joy to Thy Disciples by the promise of the Holy Spirit.
Through the blessing, they were assured
that Thou art the Son of God,
the Redeemer of the world!
troparion.label: Troparion of the Ascension

sedalion.text:
While angels gazed with wonder upon Thy dread Ascension,
and while the disciples were awestruck as Thou wast taken from earth,
O Savior, as God Thou didst ascend in glory
while the gates were raised for Thee.
For this cause then the Hosts of the heavens cried out, while marveling in amazement:
Glory to Thy descent, O Savior Christ.
Glory to Thy Kingdom's sovereignty.
Glory be to Thine Ascension,//
O Thou only Lover of mankind.
sedalion.label: Sessional Hymn (after Kathisma 1)

sedalion.text:
God the beginningless One, Who existed before all ages,
and Who took man's nature upon Himself,
and mystically deified it, was taken up on this day.
Hence, the angels ran before and indicated Him unto the apostles
as He rose with great glory to heaven's heights.
And as they worshipped Him, they cried aloud and said//
Glory be to God Who was taken up.
sedalion.label: Sessional Hymn (after Kathisma 2)

magnification.refrain:
We magnify Thee,
O Christ, the Giver of life,
and we honor Thy divine Ascension into heaven
with Thy most pure Body.
verses: Oh, clap your hands, all you peoples. Shout to God with loud songs of joy! (Ps. 46:1)
For the Lord, the Most High is terrible; a great God over all the earth. (Ps. 46:2)

sessionalHymns.text:
Having come down from heaven unto the things of earth, O Christ, as God,
with Thyself, Thou didst resurrect Adam's form,
which lay prostrate in the nether holds of Hades' vault;
in Thine Ascension to the heights
Thou didst lead it up unto the heavens and Thou didst seat it upon the throne of Thy Father,//
since Thou, the Lover of mankind, art merciful.
sessionalHymns.label: Sessional Hymn after the Polyeleios

prokeimenon.refrain: God has gone up with a shout; the Lord with the sound of a trumpet!
prokeimenon.verse: Oh, clap your hands, all you peoples. Shout to God with loud songs of joy!

gospel._note: Festal Matins Gospel of the Ascension.

postGospelSticheron.text:
Today the Powers above beheld our nature in the heavens
and marveled at the strange manner of the ascent,
in perplexity saying to one another:
"Who is this Who comes?"
But seeing their own Master,
they gave the command to lift up the heavenly gates.
With them we unceasingly sing in praise of Thee,
Who art coming again from there in the flesh
as Judge of all and God Almighty.
postGospelSticheron.label: Idiomelon of the Ascension

canon._katavasiaeNote: Katavasiae Tone 4 from the 2nd Canon of Pentecost (by John of Damascus).

ode1.irmos:
To God the Savior
Who led the people through the sea with dry feet,
and drowned Pharaoh with all his host:
to Him alone let us sing,
for He has been glorified.

troparia.refrain: Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee.
troparia.text:
O all ye peoples, let us sing a song of victory unto Christ,
Who is taken up with glory upon the shoulders of the cherubim,
and Who hath seated us together with Himself at the right hand of the Father; for He is glorified.

troparia.refrain: Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee.
troparia.text:
Beholding Christ, the Mediator between God and man, with His flesh in the heights,
the choirs of the angels were amazed,
and with one accord they sang a hymn of victory.

troparia.refrain: Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee.
troparia.text:
Let us all sing unto God, Who was seen upon Mount Sinai,
and Who gave the Law unto Moses, the seer of God,
and Who ascended from the Mount of Olives in the flesh, for He is glorified.

troparia.refrain: O Most Holy Theotokos, save us.
troparia.text:
O most pure Mother of God, do thou unceasingly intercede with Him Who assumed flesh from thee,
yet was not separated from the bosom of the Father,
that He save from every danger those whom He hath fashioned.

ode1.katavasia:
After he was covered by divine darkness,
Moses, the slow of speech, proclaimed the divinely-written law.
After he purified the eye of his mind,
he beheld the "I AM" and was taught the knowledge of the Spirit,
Whom he honored in divinely inspired song.

ode3.irmos:
By the power of Thy Cross, O Christ,
establish my understanding,
that I may hymn and glorify Thy saving Ascension.

troparia.refrain: Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee.
troparia.text:
Thou didst go up unto the Father, O Life-giving Christ,
and Thou didst exalt our race by Thine ineffable compassion, O Lover of mankind.

troparia.refrain: Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee.
troparia.text:
The orders of angels, O Savior, on beholding man's nature ascending together with Thee,
were amazed and ceaselessly praised Thee.

troparia.refrain: Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee.
troparia.text:
The choirs of angels were amazed, O Christ,
as they beheld thee taken up with Thy body,
and they praised Thy holy Ascension.

troparia.refrain: Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee.
troparia.text:
Thou didst raise up human nature which had fallen into corruption, O Christ,
and in Thine Ascension Thou didst exalt us and glorify us together with Thyself.

troparia.refrain: O Most Holy Theotokos, save us.
troparia.text:
Unceasingly entreat Him Who came forth from thy loins, O pure one,
that those who praise thee as the Mother of God may be delivered from the deception of the devil.

sedalenAfterOde3.text:
Having mounted upon heaven's clouds, O Christ,
Thou didst leave peace unto those upon the earth;
and Thou didst ascend and sit at the Father's right hand on high,
since Thou art one in essence with Him, and the Spirit, O Lord;
for though Thou hadst appeared in the flesh, without undergoing change.
Wherefore Thou dost now wait till the last consummation,
when Thou shalt return to judge all of mankind upon the earth.
O Thou most righteous Judge and Lord,
since Thou art a greatly merciful God,
do Thou spare our souls and do Thou grant to us, Thy lowly servants,//
the pardon of our failings and our sins.
sedalenAfterOde3.label: Sessional Hymn (after Ode 3)

ode4.irmos:
I have heard the report, O Lord, of the might of Thy Cross,
how Paradise was opened through it,
and I cried out: "Glory to Thy power, O Lord!"

troparia.refrain: Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee.
troparia.text:
Thou wast taken up in glory, O King of the angels,
that Thou mightest send us the Comforter from the Father.
Wherefore we cry: Glory to Thine Ascension, O Christ.

troparia.refrain: Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee.
troparia.text:
As the Savior ascended in the flesh unto the Father,
the arrays of the angels were astonished at Him
and cried aloud: Glory to Thine Ascension, O Christ.

troparia.refrain: Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee.
troparia.text:
The hosts of the angels cried unto those above: Lift up the gates for Christ our King;
Him do we praise together with the Father and the Spirit.

troparia.refrain: O Most Holy Theotokos, save us.

ode4.katavasia:
O King of Kings and only God from only God,
only Word coming forth from the Father,
as our Benefactor Thou hast sent forth without fail Thine equal and mighty Spirit onto Thine Apostles
as they sang, "Glory to Thy might, O Lord."

troparia.refrain: Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee.
troparia.text:
Having filled all things with joy, O Merciful One,
Thou didst come in Thy flesh unto the hosts on high.

troparia.refrain: Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee.
troparia.text:
As the hosts of angels saw Thee being lifted up,
they cried aloud: Lift ye the gates for our King.

troparia.refrain: Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee.
troparia.text:
As the apostles beheld the Savior being lifted up on high,
they cried with trembling: Glory be to Thee, O our King.

troparia.refrain: O Most Holy Theotokos, save us.
troparia.text:
We praise thee as a Virgin after childbirth, O Theotokos;
for thou didst conceive God the Word in the flesh for the sake of the world.

ode6.irmos:
The deep closed round about me,
the whale became my grave;
but I cried out to Thee, Who lovest mankind,
and Thy right hand saved me, O Lord.

troparia.refrain: Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee.
troparia.text:
In their hope for the coming of the Spirit, the apostles leapt for joy
as they beheld on high the Creator being lifted up,
and they cried out with fear: Glory be to Thine ascent.

troparia.refrain: Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee.
troparia.text:
The angels came and cried unto Thy disciples, O Christ:
In like manner as ye see Christ going up,
so shall He, the righteous Judge of all, come in the flesh.

troparia.refrain: Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee.
troparia.text:
As the hosts of heaven saw Thee, our Savior, being taken up into the heights together with Thy body,
they cried out, saying: Great is Thy love for mankind, O Master.

troparia.refrain: O Most Holy Theotokos, save us.
troparia.text:
O Thou bush un-burnt, and mountain and living ladder, and gate of heaven,
we glorify thee as is meet, O glorious Mary, thou boast of the Orthodox.

ode6.katavasia:
As atonement for us and salvation, O Christ,
Thou hast shone forth as Master from the Virgin,
to snatch the fallen race of Adam from corruption,
like the Prophet Jonah from the belly of the whale.

kontakion.text:
When Thou hadst fulfilled the dispensation for our sake,
and united earth to heaven,
Thou didst ascend in glory, O Christ our God,
not being parted from those who love Thee,
but remaining with them and crying:
"I am with you, and there is no one against you!"
kontakion.label: Kontakion of the Ascension

ikos.text:
Leaving the things of earth upon the earth,
and surrendering to the earth things of ashes,
come, let us come to our senses and raise our eyes and thoughts on high;
let us, O mortals, turn our gaze together with our senses up unto the heavenly gates.
Let us consider ourselves present at the Mount of Olives,
and gaze intently at the Redeemer who is riding upon a cloud;
for the Lord hath hastened up from there into the heavens.
And there the bountiful Giver of gifts distributed gifts unto His apostles,
calling to them as a Father, and strengthening them;
He guided them like Sons and said unto them:
I am not separated from you; I am with you, and no one can be against you.

ode7.irmos:
Thou didst save the Youths
who in the fiery furnace sang Thy praise:
"Blessed art Thou, the God of our fathers."

troparia.refrain: Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee.
troparia.text:
O Thou Who wast taken up on a cloud of light, Thou didst save the world,
O God of our fathers, Blessed art Thou.

troparia.refrain: Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee.
troparia.text:
O Christ, having taken upon Thy shoulders our nature, which had gone astray,
Thou didst ascend and bring it unto God the Father.

troparia.refrain: Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee.
troparia.text:
O Thou Who didst ascend in the flesh unto the bodiless Father,
O God of our fathers, Blessed art Thou.

troparia.refrain: Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee.
troparia.text:
Having raised our nature, which was deadened by sin,
Thou didst bring it unto Thine own Father, O Savior.

troparia.refrain: O Most Holy Theotokos, save us.
troparia.text:
O Thou Who wast born of the Virgin, thereby making her the Theotokos,
O God of our fathers, Blessed art Thou.

ode7.katavasia:
Horn and pipe and every kind of music raised the call
to worship a golden image without a soul,
but the light-bearing grace of the Comforter
inspires those who cry:
"O Trinity, One in Might and without beginning, blessed art Thou alone!"

ode8.irmos:
The Son and God, begotten of the Father before the ages,
and in the last times made flesh of a Virgin Mother,
you priests, extol,
and, you people, highly exalt unto all ages.

troparia.refrain: Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee.
troparia.text:
Unto Christ, the Giver of life, Who in two essences hath risen into the heavens with glory
and sitteth together with the Father,
O ye priests hymn, and ye peoples supremely exalt throughout all ages.

troparia.refrain: Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee.
troparia.text:
Unto Thee, O Savior, Who didst deliver creation from slavery to the idols,
and didst present it free unto Thine own Father,
do we give praise, and supremely exalt throughout all ages.

troparia.refrain: Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee.
O Most Holy Theotokos, save us.
troparia.text:
Thou hast proved to be more excellent than the cherubim, O pure Theotokos,
since thou hast carried in thy womb Him that rideth upon them.
Together with the bodiless ones, we mortals glorify Him throughout all ages.

ode8.katavasia:
The bonds are loosed and the flames are sprinkled with dew
in a type of the thrice-radiant Godhead.
The youths sing praise while all creation blesses its Benefactor,
the One Savior and Creator of all.
ode8._katavasiaCloser: We praise, we bless, we worship the Lord, praising and supremely exalting Him throughout all ages.

ode9.irmos:
O Thou Who art God's Mother transcending mind and word,
who ineffably in time hast given birth unto the Timeless One,
Thee do we the faithful magnify with one accord.
ode9.megalynarion:
Magnify, O my soul,
Christ the Giver of Life,
Who ascended from earth to heaven.
ode9._megalynarionNote: Sung before the irmos and as the refrain to each troparion; Magnificat is omitted at Ascension Matins.

troparia.refrain: Magnify, O my soul, Christ the Giver of Life, Who ascended from earth to heaven.
troparia.text:
As the apostles beheld Thee, Christ God, the Redeemer of the world, being exalted in a manner befitting God,
they magnified Thee with awe as they leapt for joy.

troparia.refrain: Magnify, O my soul, Christ the Giver of Life, Who ascended from earth to heaven.
troparia.text:
Beholding Thy deified flesh on high, O Christ,
the angels beckoned to one another: Truly this is our God.

troparia.refrain: Magnify, O my soul, Christ the Giver of Life, Who ascended from earth to heaven.
troparia.text:
As the orders of the Bodiless saw Thee being lifted up in the clouds, O Christ God,
they cried: Lift up the gates for the King of Glory.

troparia.refrain: Magnify, O my soul, Christ the Giver of Life, Who ascended from earth to heaven.
troparia.text:
Thee, Who didst descend unto the utmost depths of the earth,
and Who didst save man and exalt him by Thine Ascension, do we magnify.

troparia.refrain: Magnify, O my soul, Christ the Giver of Life, Who ascended from earth to heaven.
troparia.text:
Rejoice, O Theotokos, Mother of Christ God.
As thou didst behold ascending from the earth Him Whom thou didst conceive,
thou didst magnify Him together with the angels.

ode9.katavasia:
Rejoice, O Queen, glory of mothers and virgins!
No tongue, however sweet or fluent, is eloquent enough to praise thee worthily.
Every mind is overawed by thy childbearing.
Therefore, with one voice, we glorify thee.

exapostilarion.text:
With Thy disciples watching Thee, O Christ,
Thou wast taken up to the Father to take Thy seat with Him.
Angels ran forward crying out:
"Lift up the gates, lift them up!
For the King has gone up to the glory, the source of light."
exapostilarion.label: Exapostilarion of the Ascension

stichera.verse: Praise Him for His mighty deeds; praise Him according to His exceeding greatness! (Ps. 150:2)
Praise Him with trumpet sound; praise Him with lute and harp! (Ps. 150:3)
Praise Him with timbrel and dance; praise Him with strings and pipe! (Ps. 150:4)
stichera.text:
The leaders of the Angels
witnessed the strangeness of Thine ascent, O Savior,
and said to one another in perplexity: "What is this sight?
He Whom we see is human in form,
yet as God He rises far above the heavens
ascending there in the flesh."

stichera.verse: Praise Him with sounding cymbals; praise Him with loud clashing cymbals! Let everything that breathes praise the Lord! (Ps. 150:5)
stichera.text:
The men of Galilee saw Thee, O Word,
taken up from the mount of Olives in Thy body,
and heard Angels crying out to them:
"Why do you stand gazing? This Jesus will come again in the flesh
in the same way as you have seen Him."

doxastikon.text:
Thou wast born, as Thou Thyself didst will,
and didst appear as Thou Thyself didst desire;
Thou didst suffer in the flesh, O our God,
and didst rise from the dead, having trampled on death.
Thou wast taken up in glory, filling all things,
and Thou didst send us the Divine Spirit,
that we may praise and glorify Thy Godhead.
doxastikon.author: Doxastikon of the Ascension

troparionAfterDoxology.text:
Thou didst ascend in glory, O Christ our God,
granting joy to Thy Disciples by the promise of the Holy Spirit.
Through the blessing, they were assured
that Thou art the Son of God,
the Redeemer of the world!
